grammar.notation: ? optional; | alternatives; HOLE[T] missing typed operand. Calendar lexicon uses generic months/weekdays/number/ordinal forms, never customer/test values.

productions.rule: CALENDAR := MONTH (THE? DAY)? YEAR? | DAY OF MONTH YEAR? | ISO_DATE | WEEKDAY CALENDAR?
productions.detail: MONTH alone may close; MONTH THE requires DAY or emits HOLE[day]. Optional comma belongs inside only when followed by a supported year. Calendar validity is separate: impossible day can be complete language.

productions.rule: NTH := DET? (ORDINAL | LAST | FIRST) (WEEKDAY | WORKING DAY) (OF | IN) (MONTH | PERIOD | REF | HOLE[period])
productions.detail: Also recognize ordinal weekday without of/in as reference-dependent; do not detach ordinal as a second candidate. Retain connector when its operand is absent.

productions.rule: OFFSET := COUNT (BUSINESS | WORKING)? DAYS (BEFORE | AFTER | FOLLOWING) OPERAND
productions.detail: OPERAND := CALENDAR | NTH | REF | EVENT | HOLE[temporal]. Reference that/it is syntactically present without resolved value.

productions.rule: REL := TEMPORAL (BEFORE | AFTER | FOLLOWING | NEAREST TO) OPERAND | (BEFORE | AFTER | UNTIL) OPERAND
productions.detail: following and nearest-to must retain operators; generic before administrative event is event_time/admin-time, not automatically a payment date. Terminal bare relation is open, not absence.

productions.rule: RANGE := BETWEEN OPERAND AND OPERAND | FROM OPERAND (TO | UNTIL) OPERAND
productions.detail: Both endpoints form one node. A missing connector/second endpoint emits a typed hole, retaining from/between and any completed endpoint. No dates selected/normalized from a range.
Only when both operands are temporal or the second is a typed missing temporal operand; ordinary administrative OR remains a separate act. Missing endpoint remains in maximal expression.

productions.rule: REF := THAT DATE | ANOTHER DATE | THAT DAY | THAT WEEK | FOLLOWING MONTH | THAT | IT | THOSE TWO EVENTS
productions.detail: Bare that/it accepted only in a temporal operand position. Closed linguistic reference, reference_mask=false unless independent resolver later proves it. This is not a permission label.

productions.rule: EVENT := supported subject-event predicate | THE DAY supported subject-event predicate | event noun GERUND | pronoun supported predicate
productions.detail: Implement only finite source-generic event productions in slice3: e.g. the statement arrives/arriving, it closes, the plan resumes, that happens. Preserve unknown words in unsupported operand span; do not greedily consume arbitrary clauses to make a closed node.

productions.rule: EXTREMUM := (BY)? WHICHEVER IS (LATER | EARLIER), (EVENT OR EVENT | REF | HOLE[event])
productions.detail: Slice3 extension, not needed for initial calendar/range repair. Operator affects value constraint and stays in semantic extent.

productions.rule: BOUND := (BY | UNTIL | BEFORE | AFTER) TEMPORAL; ATTACH := (ON | FOR) TEMPORAL
productions.detail: BY/UNTIL are semantic bound nodes. ON/FOR may be attachment only under a recognized parent grammar; for plan X is a target phrase, not a date wrapper. No unconditional prefix stripping.

productions.rule: DEICTIC := NOW | LATER | AT THIS POINT | AT ONCE | FOR A MOMENT
productions.detail: Optional event/admin temporal proposals. Value remains vague; no target/payment fact assigned merely from payment phase. Separate accounting prevents gaming calendar recall by changing task scope.

grammar.limits: Retain R4 source/candidate/expression/token/locale limits. Use memoized non-left-recursive parser with precedence and a finite agenda of typed spans. No runtime label files, model predictions, author metadata or annotation offsets as inputs.
grammar.maximality: Remove a child from top-level candidates only if it is a verified child of the same typed parent with compatible source scope. Containment alone does not erase independent correction, target or clause nodes. Keep child spans in the graph.

boundary_projection_laws.law: Source immutability: every semantic/attachment/marker span is a slice of the unchanged delivered source. Use codepoint offsets; UTF8 byte offsets are derived, never mixed.
Lossless projection: reconstructed raw extent equals original source slice after reinserting all classified removed segments. Projection is idempotent under its pinned grammar.
Never remove before/after/by/until/from/between/either/and/or/of/in/following/nearest-to when owned by temporal production, nor unfinished determiners, range tails or ellipsis.
A trailing delimiter comma may leave semantic extent only if it is outside every consumed year/event production. Internal comma before supported year remains; quotes retain quotation-role evidence.

Projected equivalence requires same source event, ordered operands, operator types/spans, holes, role/polarity scope, target dependency and marker interpretation. Shared endpoint text is insufficient.

Literal exact and projected-equivalent are separately reported. Do not replace frozen V7 spans, assign nearest-overlap labels, or count projected matches as new admitted examples without independently reviewed new alignment policy.

Discontinuous source interruptions are represented as segments and unsupported dependency initially. The long interjection in TRAIN primary11 remains masked; no clipping or removal may turn it into a falsely complete date.
Target propagation is monotone only along source-proven parent/child binding. A composite range with unknown target stays unknown; annotation target sets are not copied into generated candidates.

equivalence_and_ablation_plan.review_policy: Use current annotations as diagnostic source spans only. New parser outputs are constructed solely from raw text. If source annotation and grammar extent differ, flag for independent source re-review in a NEW version; do not edit old annotations or nearest-match them into supervision. Projected equivalence does not certify semantic correctness.
equivalence_and_ablation_plan.acceptance: Reject any semantic operator/hole/privacy/target/correction regression in specified finite cases; report actual TRAIN tradeoffs rather than invent a required recall percentage. A useful repair is one whose exact candidate recovery is shown without false financial commitment or mask bypass; actual corpus counts remain future measurements.
equivalence_and_ablation_plan.generalization: Any improvements after observing these TRAIN errors are development results. Freeze parser before genuinely new author/source-regression collection; keep DEV/qualification unread. Grammar-case passes do not establish robust unseen-language coverage.
equivalence_and_ablation_plan.training_readiness: After new extraction, independently resolve ancestry and schema in source-compatible new artifacts, recount eligible canonical support under existing floors and per-fold admission, obtain fresh parent authorization.
